heroHeadline: Trump Returns From Ireland to Campaign for Midterms, Dismisses AI Slowdown Call and China-Iran Satellite Report
heroSubtitle: President Trump returned to the US Monday, September 14, 2026 (Day 603), to campaign for Republican midterm candidates, telling reporters he doesn't know whether Congress must approve his pledged $5,000-per-adult 'Trump dividend' but that it's 'easy enough if the Republicans win.' Aboard Air Force One he downplayed a Wall Street Journal report that Iran obtained satellite imagery of a Jordan air base from Chinese entities before a July strike killed three US soldiers there, saying 'we spy on them too.' The developments followed a Sunday, September 13 press availability at his Doonbeg, Ireland golf resort where Trump floated an open-ended US troop presence in Iran to 'keep the oil, like Venezuela,' and dismissed a joint call from the CEOs of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI to slow AI development, saying 'whoever wins AI, wins.' Separately, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' August CPI report (released Sep 11) showed inflation cooling to 3.4% year-over-year from April's three-year high of 3.8%, while Trump's approval rating held roughly flat in the mid-to-high 30s across pollster aggregates ahead of the November midterms.
